subject: chemistry
title: ZIMSEC O-Level Chemistry

officialDocument.title: O Level Chemistry Syllabus, Forms 3 - 4, 2015 - 2022 (Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education, Curriculum Development and Technical Services), examined by ZIMSEC at O Level
officialDocument.publisher: Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education (Curriculum Development and Technical Services) / Zimbabwe School Examinations Council (ZIMSEC)

sourceNote: Section, topic and subtopic headings are transcribed from the Ministry's O Level Chemistry Syllabus Forms 3 - 4 (2015 - 2022): sections and topics with their numbers from '6.0 Topics' and '7.0 Scope and sequence chart' (7.1.0 to 7.4.4), subtopics from the scope and sequence chart and the '8.0 Competency matrix', each grouped under its topic with its Form. Learning-objective statements are our own paraphrase of the competency matrix; their codes (topic number + running number) are ours, not the board's.
notes: Source status (checked 2026-10-07): the full text of the Ministry document 'O Level Chemistry Syllabus Forms 3 - 4, 2015 - 2022' (Curriculum Development and Technical Services, (c) 2015, 40 pages) was read from a copy hosted at https://zimsake.co.zw/softidrive/download/0/sh/aa1838cc2e57c7a469685ff246a70d33, which is not an official Ministry or ZIMSEC address. The topic list, the scope and sequence chart, every competency-matrix row and the assessment section were read. Replace the officialDocument URL with an official download address once one is confirmed.

Curriculum change: the Heritage-Based Curriculum Framework 2024-2030 is replacing the 2015-2022 framework in phases. Secondary reports (a published summary of a Ministry circular and press articles, not checked against the circular itself) say Forms 1, 2, 3 and 5 began it in 2025 with full implementation in 2026; The Herald (12 January 2025) reported that Form 4 candidates in 2025 were still examined on the 2015-2022 framework, and (4 August 2026) that the June 2026 ZIMSEC session was the last conducted under the old (competency-based) curriculum. November 2026 and later O-Level candidates may therefore be examined on a Heritage-Based Chemistry syllabus for Forms 3-4, which could not be obtained. Confirm, add the new syllabus as a new version file and give this version an effectiveTo; the concept registry is shared, so content written for this version carries over.

Version dates and code: assumed first examined in November 2018 (effectiveFrom 2018-01-01), in line with the family's other ZIMSEC 2015-2022 syllabi. The subject code is not printed in the document (code left null): confirm it.

Numbering: sections and topics carry the scope and sequence chart numbers (7.1.0 to 7.4.0 and 7.1.1 to 7.4.4); the chart misprints Atoms, elements and compounds as '2.1.3', recorded here as 7.1.3. Subtopic codes are left empty because the competency-matrix numbers are incomplete or inconsistent (Matter, Contact process, Ostwald process, Lime in agriculture and construction and Qualitative analysis are unnumbered, Rates of reaction is numbered 8.10.0, and continuation rows repeat numbers); each subtopic description gives its Form and its matrix number where one is printed.
Two Laboratory techniques subtopics are both headed 'Separation techniques' (Form 3 and Form 4); the node names add the Form to tell them apart.

The scope and sequence chart lists 'Industrial applications' (Form 4) under both Equilibria and Reaction kinetics; the competency matrix has a single subtopic, 'Industrial applications of reaction kinetics and equilibria' (8.23.2), under Equilibria, which is where it is recorded.

The scope and sequence chart names the Form 4 electrochemistry subtopic 'Electrolytic purification of copper and aluminium', but its competency-matrix row (8.21.2) describes only copper; the aluminium-extraction concept is tagged to this subtopic and needs confirmation.

Assessment (section 8.0 of the document): the final grade is 30% continuous assessment and 70% summative assessment. Paper 1: 40 compulsory four-option multiple-choice items, 1 hour, 40 marks, 20%. Paper 2: theory, 2 hours, 100 marks, 40%; Section A has five compulsory 8-mark structured questions and Section B five 15-mark structured questions of which candidates answer any four; a Periodic Table is printed in Papers 1 and 2. Paper 3: practical test of two compulsory 20-mark questions, with candidates assessed as they work; its duration and weighting are not printed (70% - 60% suggests 10%: confirm). Continuous assessment: practical tests, theory tests and a project (only the Form 3 row, 10%, is printed). Press reports say continuous assessment was replaced by school-based projects under the Heritage-Based Curriculum: confirm the current scheme.

Not in the Forms 3-4 document, so these Cambridge-only concepts of the family are not covered here: Group I (alkali metals), rusting and its prevention, proton transfer and strong and weak acids, hydrated salts and water of crystallisation, physical and chemical changes (assumed from Forms 1-2 Combined Science), hydrogen-oxygen fuel cells and enthalpy changes from bond energies. Confirm, particularly for rusting and for strong and weak acids, which O-Level papers often assume.

Coverage decisions to confirm: giant covalent structures (diamond, graphite) are not named in the matrix but are tagged to Covalent bonding because diamond processing and graphite electrodes appear elsewhere in the syllabus; the general principles of electrolysis (including molten compounds) are tagged to Electrolysis of acidified water; planning investigations and handling data (assessment objective 3, Paper 3) are tagged to Measuring instruments; collision-theory explanations are taught with Factors affecting rates of reaction; fermentation is tagged only to Alcohols > Fermentation although Production of fuels also lists it; chromatography (including Rf values from Form 4) is tagged to the Form 3 Separation techniques subtopic.
The pollution subtopic lists 'shakers' among the methods of controlling pollution; this is probably a misprint for scrubbers and is left out of the objectives until confirmed.

The document lists suggested site visits (for example Sable Chemicals, Zimphos, Empress mine, Bikita Minerals, Hwange, Green Fuels); these are suggested activities, not examinable content, and are not transcribed.
overview: ZIMSEC O-Level Chemistry (Forms 3 and 4) builds understanding of chemical concepts and principles and their safe, environmentally responsible use in everyday life and in Zimbabwe's industries, including mining and mineral beneficiation, fertiliser and acid manufacture, fuels, water treatment and waste management. Its content is grouped into physical, inorganic, organic and environmental chemistry, emphasises practical and enterprise skills, and assumes the Forms 1 and 2 Combined Science course.
assessmentOverview: Under this syllabus the final grade combines continuous assessment (30%) with three examination papers (70%): Paper 1, multiple choice (1 hour, 40 marks, 20%); Paper 2, structured theory questions (2 hours, 100 marks, 40%); and Paper 3, a practical test of two 20-mark questions. Confirm the current scheme, because continuous assessment has been replaced by school-based projects under the Heritage-Based Curriculum.

components.name: Paper 1: Multiple choice
components.description: 40 compulsory multiple-choice items, each with four options. A Periodic Table is printed in the paper.

components.name: Paper 2: Theory
components.description: Section A (40 marks): five compulsory structured questions of 8 marks. Section B (60 marks): five structured questions of 15 marks, of which candidates answer any four. A Periodic Table is printed in the paper.

components.name: Paper 3: Practical test
components.description: Two compulsory practical questions of 20 marks each; candidates are assessed as they carry out the practical. Duration and weighting are not printed in the syllabus.

components.name: Continuous assessment
components.description: School-based practical tests, theory tests and a project during Forms 3 and 4 (30% of the final grade under this syllabus). Reported to have been replaced by school-based projects under the Heritage-Based Curriculum: confirm.

children.name: Measuring instruments
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.1.2).

objectives.text: Identify suitable apparatus for measuring time, temperature, mass, volume and distance, such as stop-watches, thermometers, balances, burettes, pipettes, measuring cylinders and gas syringes.
Use measuring apparatus correctly to take and record measurements.

children.name: Separation techniques (Form 3)
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.1.3): filtration, distillation, crystallisation, evaporation, and paper and thin-layer chromatography.

objectives.text: Identify methods of separating mixtures, including filtration, distillation, crystallisation, evaporation, and paper and thin-layer chromatography.
Suggest a suitable separation technique from the nature of a mixture.

children.name: Volumetric analysis
children.description: Form 4 (competency matrix 8.17.2).

objectives.text: Carry out acid-base titrations and complete titration tables.
Calculate amounts in moles and concentrations from titration results.

children.name: Separation techniques (Form 4)
children.description: Form 4 (competency matrix 8.17.3): fractional distillation, steam distillation, paper and thin-layer chromatography and Rf values.

objectives.text: Describe the principles of fractional distillation and steam distillation.
Describe paper and thin-layer chromatography and calculate Rf values.

children.name: Qualitative analysis
children.description: Form 4 (unnumbered row after 8.17.3 in the competency matrix).

objectives.text: Carry out tests to identify the cations Al³⁺, NH₄⁺, Mg²⁺, Pb²⁺, Cu²⁺, Fe²⁺, Fe³⁺, Cr³⁺ and Zn²⁺ and the anions Cl⁻, I⁻, NO₃⁻, SO₄²⁻ and CO₃²⁻.
Describe tests to identify the gases ammonia, carbon dioxide, chlorine, hydrogen, oxygen and sulfur dioxide.

children.name: States of matter
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.2.0): states of matter, kinetic theory, changes of state and diffusion.

objectives.text: State the three states of matter.
Explain the states of matter using the kinetic theory.
Explain changes from one state of matter to another in terms of energy and the arrangement of particles.
Describe and explain diffusion.

children.name: Heating and cooling curves
children.description: Form 4 (competency matrix 8.18.1), including the effect of impurities on melting and boiling points.

objectives.text: Interpret heating and cooling curves.
Describe how impurities affect melting points and boiling points.

children.name: Atomic structure
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.3.1).

objectives.text: Describe the protons, neutrons and electrons that make up an atom and draw diagrams to show the structure of atoms.

children.name: Elements and compounds
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.3.2, headed 'Elements'): chemical symbols, atomic and mass numbers, nuclide notation, electronic configuration of the first 20 elements and isotopes.

objectives.text: Represent elements by their chemical symbols.
Use and interpret nuclide notation, working out the numbers of protons, neutrons and electrons from atomic numbers and mass numbers.
Deduce the electronic configuration of an element (first 20 elements) from given data and show it in a dot-and-cross diagram.
Explain the concept of an isotope.

children.name: Covalent bonding
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.3.3).

objectives.text: Describe how a covalent bond forms and draw dot-and-cross diagrams for molecules such as H₂, Cl₂, O₂, N₂, HCl, H₂O, CH₄, CO₂ and NH₃.

children.name: Ionic bonding
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.3.3).

objectives.text: Describe how ionic bonds form between metals and non-metals and draw dot-and-cross diagrams for compounds such as NaCl, MgO and Al₂O₃.
Deduce the chemical formula of a compound from a dot-and-cross diagram.
Distinguish ionic from covalent compounds by their properties, such as melting point, boiling point, electrical conductivity and solubility.

children.name: Metallic bonding
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.3.3).

objectives.text: Describe metallic bonding as a lattice of positive ions in a 'sea' of delocalised electrons.
Relate the physical properties of metals to metallic bonding.

children.name: Mole concept
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.4.1): the mole, relative atomic and molecular masses, molar mass and concentration of solutions.

objectives.text: Describe the mole concept, relative atomic mass, relative molecular mass and molar mass.
Calculate amounts in moles from masses, masses from amounts, relative molecular masses and concentrations of solutions.

children.name: Percentage composition
children.description: Form 4 (competency matrix 8.19.1), including empirical and molecular formulae.

objectives.text: Calculate the percentage composition of elements in compounds and ores, for example haematite, copper pyrites, bauxite, fertilisers and ores of the platinum-group metals.
Calculate empirical and molecular formulae.

children.name: Molar gas volume
children.description: Form 4 (competency matrix 8.19.2); the molar gas volume is taken as 24 dm³ at room temperature and pressure.

objectives.text: Explain the concept of molar gas volume (24 dm³ per mole at room temperature and pressure).
Use the molar gas volume in calculations.

children.name: Chemical equations
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.5.1).

objectives.text: Write balanced chemical equations.
Calculate the masses and volumes of products from given quantities of reactants, and the reverse.
Determine the limiting reagent from given data.

children.name: Percentage yield and purity
children.description: Form 4 (competency matrix 8.20.1).

objectives.text: Calculate percentage yield and percentage purity.
Explain the difference between actual yield and theoretical yield.

children.name: Properties of acids and bases
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.6.1): acids, bases, the pH scale, acid-base indicators and oxides.

objectives.text: Identify the properties of acids and bases, including their effect on acid-base indicators and their pH.
Classify oxides as acidic, basic or amphoteric, for example calcium oxide, sodium oxide, aluminium oxide, sulfur trioxide, carbon dioxide and nitrogen dioxide.

children.name: Preparation of salts
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.6.2): neutralisation, displacement and precipitation.

objectives.text: Describe methods of preparing salts by neutralisation, displacement and precipitation, for example by reacting acids with alkalis, metal oxides, carbonates and metals.

children.name: Redox reactions
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.7.1).

objectives.text: Define oxidation and reduction in terms of electron transfer and of changes in oxidation number.
Identify oxidising agents and reducing agents.

children.name: Cells and batteries
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.7.2).

objectives.text: Identify the parts of a simple cell (electrodes and electrolyte).
Describe the reactions at the electrodes of a simple cell.
Describe the composition and maintenance of a lead-acid battery.

children.name: Electrolysis of acidified water
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.7.3).

objectives.text: Describe the electrolysis of acidified water.
Identify the products of the electrolysis of water and state their uses.
Deduce the formula of water from the ratio of the volumes of the gases produced.

children.name: Redox equations
children.description: Form 4 (competency matrix 8.21.1).

objectives.text: Construct balanced redox equations, for example for displacement reactions and for the reactions at electrodes.

children.name: Electrolytic purification of copper and aluminium
children.description: Form 4 (competency matrix 8.21.2, which describes copper only; aluminium is named in the scope and sequence chart).

objectives.text: Describe the electrolytic cell used to purify copper, the uses of copper and the by-products of the process.

children.name: Endothermic and exothermic reactions
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.8.1).

objectives.text: Describe endothermic and exothermic reactions in terms of bond breaking and bond forming.
Distinguish between endothermic and exothermic reactions, for example burning fuels, neutralisation and dissolving ammonium nitrate.

children.name: Energy profile diagrams
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.8.2).

objectives.text: Draw energy profile diagrams for endothermic and exothermic reactions.
Interpret energy profile diagrams.

children.name: Enthalpy changes
children.description: Form 4 (competency matrix 8.22.1): enthalpy changes of combustion, neutralisation and solution.

objectives.text: Describe the concept of enthalpy change, including enthalpy changes of combustion, neutralisation and solution.
Determine enthalpy changes by experiment.
Calculate enthalpy changes using q = mcΔT, taking the mass of a solution from its volume.

children.name: Reversible reactions
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.9.1).

objectives.text: Explain the term reversible reaction and use the ⇌ sign in equations.
Analyse reversible reactions and predict the effect of changing the conditions of a reversible reaction at equilibrium.

children.name: Dynamic equilibrium
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.9.2).

objectives.text: Explain the term dynamic equilibrium.

children.name: Haber process
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.9.3).

objectives.text: Describe how the raw materials for the Haber process, nitrogen and hydrogen, are produced.
Explain the conditions used in the Haber process.
State the uses of ammonia.
Describe safety precautions and the environmental impacts of ammonia production.

children.name: Contact process
children.description: Form 3 (unnumbered row after 8.9.3 in the competency matrix).

objectives.text: Identify the sources of the raw materials for the Contact process.
Describe the Contact process and explain the conditions used.
State the uses of sulfuric acid.
Describe the environmental impacts of sulfuric acid production.

children.name: Ostwald process
children.description: Form 3 (unnumbered row in the competency matrix).

objectives.text: Identify the sources of the raw materials for the Ostwald process.
Describe the Ostwald process and explain the conditions used.
State the uses of nitric acid.
Describe the environmental impacts of nitric acid production.

children.name: Production of fertilisers
children.description: Form 4 (competency matrix 8.23.1): ammonium nitrate and ammonium sulfate.

objectives.text: Describe the manufacture of ammonium nitrate and ammonium sulfate fertilisers.

children.name: Industrial applications of reaction kinetics and equilibria
children.description: Form 4 (competency matrix 8.23.2); the scope and sequence chart also lists it under Reaction kinetics.

objectives.text: Link the reaction conditions of the Haber and Contact processes to production costs.
Analyse the cost of production in relation to the cost of the product.
Justify the conditions chosen for the Haber and Contact processes.

children.name: Rates of reaction
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.10.0, the first row of 8.10).

objectives.text: Describe methods of measuring reaction rates, using changes in volume, mass or colour with time.
Deduce the rate of a reaction from graphs.
Calculate rates of reaction from given information.

children.name: Factors affecting rates of reaction
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.10.2): temperature, concentration, surface area, catalysts, pressure and stirring.

objectives.text: Describe how temperature, concentration, surface area, catalysts, pressure and stirring affect the rate of a reaction.

children.name: Periodic trends
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.11.2).

objectives.text: Describe the change from metallic to non-metallic character across a period.
Explain the relationship between the number of electron shells and the period.

children.name: Group trends (Groups II and VII)
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.11.3).

objectives.text: Describe the relationship between group number and the number of valence electrons.
Describe the reactions of magnesium, calcium and barium with oxygen and with water.
Describe the trends in the physical properties (colour, physical state and volatility) and the chemical properties of the Group VII elements.

children.name: Transition elements
children.description: Form 4 (competency matrix 8.24.2): copper, iron, manganese, cobalt, chromium, nickel and vanadium.

objectives.text: Describe the properties of the transition elements copper, iron, manganese, cobalt, chromium, nickel and vanadium.
Explain the industrial and biological importance of transition elements, for example in catalysis, haemoglobin and alloys.

children.name: Properties of metals and non-metals
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.12.1).

objectives.text: Compare the physical properties of metals and non-metals: malleability, ductility, thermal and electrical conductivity, melting and boiling points, density and lustre.
Explain the differences in the physical properties of metals and non-metals.

children.name: Reactivity series
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.12.2), including displacement reactions.

objectives.text: Show the reactivity of metals by experiment, including reactions with water and dilute acids and displacement reactions.
Arrange elements in order of reactivity.
Use the reactivity series to explain electroplating, electrochemical cells and the extraction of metals.

children.name: Lime in agriculture and construction
children.description: Form 3 (unnumbered row in the competency matrix).

objectives.text: Describe the production of calcium oxide (lime) from calcium carbonate (limestone).
Explain the uses of calcium oxide in agriculture and construction.

children.name: Composition of mineral ores
children.description: Form 4 (competency matrix 8.25.1): ores of iron, copper, platinum, lithium, nickel and gold.

objectives.text: Describe the composition of the mineral ores of iron, copper, platinum, lithium, nickel and gold.

children.name: Extraction of metals
children.description: Form 4 (competency matrix 8.25.2): the blast furnace; purification of copper, nickel, platinum and gold; value addition and beneficiation; uses of metals and alloys.

objectives.text: Describe methods of processing minerals, including the blast furnace and the purification of copper, nickel, platinum and gold, and the meaning of value addition and beneficiation.
Explain the uses of metals and alloys, including alloys of copper, iron and aluminium, in terms of their properties.

children.name: Processing of diamond and coal
children.description: Form 4 (competency matrix 8.25.3).

objectives.text: Describe the processing of diamond and coal, including the destructive distillation and gasification of coal, and the value addition and beneficiation of these resources.

children.name: Liquefaction and fractional distillation of air
children.description: Form 4 (competency matrix 8.25.4), including the composition of air.

objectives.text: Describe the liquefaction and fractional distillation of air.
Identify the uses of oxygen, nitrogen, carbon dioxide and the noble gases.

children.name: Types of fuels
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.13.2): solid, liquid and gaseous fuels.

objectives.text: Classify fuels according to their physical state as solid, liquid or gaseous fuels.

children.name: Production of fuels
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.13.3): fermentation, fractional distillation of crude oil, destructive distillation of coal and wood, and biodiesel.

objectives.text: Describe the process of fermentation as a source of fuel.
Outline the fractional distillation of crude oil.
Describe the destructive distillation of coal and of wood.
Describe the production of biodiesel from jatropha oil.

children.name: Fuel efficiency
children.description: Form 4 (competency matrix 8.26.2).

objectives.text: Determine the heating values of fuels by experiment.
Explain why some fuels are more efficient than others.

children.name: Classification and nomenclature of organic compounds
Homologous series
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.14.1): hydrocarbons, alcohols and carboxylic acids with up to six carbon atoms.

objectives.text: Define the term homologous series.
Name organic compounds systematically.
Classify organic compounds with up to six carbon atoms as hydrocarbons, alcohols or carboxylic acids.

children.name: Isomerism
children.description: Form 4 (competency matrix 8.27.1): structural isomers of alkanes with up to six carbon atoms.

objectives.text: Describe the term isomerism.
Identify the structural isomers of alkanes with up to six carbon atoms and draw their structures.

children.name: Alkanes and alkenes
children.description: Form 4 (competency matrix 8.28.1).

objectives.text: Describe the manufacture of alkanes and alkenes, including the cracking of long-chain alkanes.
Distinguish between alkanes and alkenes, for example with bromine water.
Describe the chemical properties of alkanes as shown by methane: combustion and reaction with chlorine in ultraviolet light and in the dark.
Describe the chemical properties of alkenes as shown by ethene: combustion and reactions with bromine water, steam and hydrogen.

children.name: Fermentation
children.description: Form 4 (competency matrix 8.29.1), including traditional fermentation in Zimbabwe.

objectives.text: Describe the conditions necessary for fermentation.
Describe the industrial production of ethanol by fermentation.

children.name: Properties of ethanol
children.description: Form 4 (competency matrix 8.29.2).

objectives.text: Describe the properties of ethanol: solubility, boiling point, combustion, oxidation to a carboxylic acid and dehydration to ethene.
Describe the uses and social effects of ethanol.

children.name: Chemistry of carboxylic acids
children.description: Form 4 (competency matrix 8.30.1), including esterification and soap making.

objectives.text: Describe the formation of ethanoic acid by the oxidation of ethanol.
Describe the chemical properties of carboxylic acids, including esterification and reaction with carbonates.
Describe the uses of ethanoic acid, for example in making perfumes, preserving food and flavouring.
Describe saponification (soap making), the structure of a soap molecule and the by-product glycerol.

children.name: Synthetic polymers
children.description: Form 4 (competency matrix 8.31.1): polythene, nylon and Terylene; condensation polymers drawn as block diagrams.

objectives.text: Describe the formation of polythene by addition polymerisation.
Describe the formation of nylon and Terylene by condensation polymerisation.
Draw structures to represent synthetic polymers (block diagrams for condensation polymers) and identify their repeat units and linkages.
Deduce the structure of the monomer from a given polymer, and the reverse.
Describe the uses of synthetic polymers.

children.name: Natural polymers
children.description: Form 4 (competency matrix 8.31.2): starch and proteins.

objectives.text: Name the type of linkage in starch and in proteins.
Draw structures to represent natural polymers and deduce the monomer from a given polymer, and the reverse.
Describe the hydrolysis of natural polymers.

children.name: Classification of waste
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.15.2).

objectives.text: Identify solid, liquid and gaseous waste, and biodegradable and non-biodegradable waste.
Identify the different sources of waste, including household and industrial waste.
Describe methods of identifying wastes from industries.
Suggest ways of controlling waste.

children.name: Effects of waste on the environment
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.15.3): eutrophication, acid rain, global warming, health effects and ozone-layer depletion.

objectives.text: Describe the effects of waste on the environment, including eutrophication, acid rain, global warming, effects on health and depletion of the ozone layer.

children.name: Waste disposal methods
children.description: Form 4 (competency matrix 8.32.2): incineration, landfills and activated sludge; reuse and recycling.

objectives.text: Identify waste disposal methods, including incineration, landfills and activated sludge.
Describe the advantages and disadvantages of each method of waste disposal.
Explain the reuse and recycling of waste.

children.name: Sources of pollutants
children.description: Form 4 (competency matrix 8.33.1): sources, effects and control of pollution.

objectives.text: List the sources of pollutants, including industrial waste, exhaust fumes and domestic waste.
Explain the effects of pollution: acid rain, eutrophication, global warming, health hazards and depletion of the ozone layer.
Describe methods of controlling pollution, such as catalytic converters and recycling.

children.name: Quality of water from different sources
children.description: Form 3 (competency matrix 8.16.1, headed 'Composition of water from different sources'): dams, boreholes, rivers and rain; hard and soft water.

objectives.text: Describe the composition of water from different sources, such as dams, boreholes, rivers and rain, comparing colour, smell and pH.
Distinguish between hard and soft water.
Describe the effects of hard water on boilers, electric kettles, geysers and water pipes and on the lathering of soap.

children.name: Purification of water
children.description: Form 4 (competency matrix 8.34.1): filtration, flocculation, sedimentation and chlorination.

objectives.text: Describe the large-scale purification of water by filtration, flocculation, sedimentation and chlorination.
Explain the roles of aluminium sulfate and chlorine in the treatment of water.

children.name: Herbs in health and agriculture
children.description: Form 4 (competency matrix 8.35.1).

objectives.text: Describe the uses of herbs in health and agriculture.
Describe the advantages and disadvantages of using herbs.
